Product: 'Round-ups', a tool in the Nationwide Banking App. Jurisdiction: UK (Nationwide Building Society). Checked 2026-10-13. Eligibility: holders of a Nationwide current account. Method: debit card transactions are rounded up to the nearest pound (fixed £1 unit, no multiplier, no fixed amount per purchase). Timing: the app works out the spare change, then the member transfers the last 7 days of it in one go. Nothing is swept automatically. Unknown, because no terms, FAQ or conditions document was found: which savings accounts qualify, the opt-in steps, which purchases are excluded, what happens with insufficient funds, refunds and closure. The app demo (nationwidedemo.co.uk) is rendered by JavaScript and could not be read. SLATE has no roundUp for gb-nationwide, and that is correct. In SLATE's engine, any roundUp words turn on an automatic nightly transfer (roundUpsOn in src/engine/systems/accountlife.ts; the nightly post is at lines 226-233). Adding Nationwide's words would make SLATE move money that Nationwide never moves by itself. SLATE cannot express a manual round-up. That is the only gap.

On the same page, Quick save is a separate tool ("move money ... in just a couple of taps"). nationwide.co.uk/savings/instant-access-savings-accounts: "save your change using round-ups and quick save with a Nationwide current account." The 2019 press release says only '5 de los comercios más utilizados', meaning convenience stores and fast-food chains. The merchant names that circulate (OXXO, Starbucks and others) come from non-official sites only. For Disfruta y guarda, the timing, insufficient funds, refunds and closure are all unknown, as they are for Redondeo.
